answer: For a poll on an opal sculpture beneath a plume over the dune, officials check election-bound signatures on a submitted ring of at least 10 distinct applicant keys. They issue one ballot per key only if every key signs its successor in a single closed ring; otherwise they refuse the ring. An attacker must create and sign with 10 keys to qualify alone, costing effort. One person can control every key, so automation makes this weak.
